correctness.rationale: At a positive equilibrium, one successor entry per row of BX is negative and strictly dominates the sum of every other nonnegative entry by a_i>0. Every convex homotopy to the pure signed n-cycle remains strictly row-diagonally dominant after permuting columns, hence nonsingular. At the pure cycle the determinant equals minus the product of all strictly positive successor magnitudes for every n, forcing det(BX)<0. The full equilibrium Jacobian equals -XB and its real monic characteristic polynomial changes sign between zero and positive infinity, yielding a strictly positive real eigenvalue. Invertibility of B establishes uniqueness conditional on existence. Exact-rational independent checks verify 84 heterogeneous examples and 13 uniform witnesses; the all-order proof does not depend on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The 2023 impossible-ecologies study proves the three-species cycle but states that analogous four- and five-species impossible ecologies are based on numerical evidence and conjectures infinite impossible families. This theorem proves the one-benefactor predator-cycle family in every finite order, including a negative full Jacobian determinant and a positive real unstable eigenvalue. The related D-stability subcommunity exclusion theorem concerns relations between different communities, not universal single-community cyclic impossibility. Bibliographic incompleteness remains a risk.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023 ecological-topology work identifies no general analytical treatment of its conjectured infinite families of impossible cyclic predation networks. The result settles a natural whole family for every population size, shows an exact negative determinant and real unstable eigenvalue even when a positive coexistence equilibrium exists, and distinguishes feasibility from stability structurally. It does not rely on an arbitrary enumerative slice or a slight numerical improvement.
